record.original_question: Classify all pairs of polytopes P and Q for which the amalgamation class ⟨P, Q⟩ is nonempty and the number of flag orbits of polytopes in that class is bounded.

evidence.quote: Problem 17. Classify all pairs of polytopes P and Q such that hP, Qi is non-empty and the number of flag orbits of polytopes in hP, Qi is bounded.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope is a graded partially ordered set (with a minimum and maximum element) whose maximal chains, called flags, all have the same length and which satisfies the standard diamond condition and strong flag-connectedness used to define abstract polytopes. The automorphism group Γ(P) of a polytope P acts on its set of flags, and the flags fall into orbits under this action; the number of such orbits is the flag-orbit count of P.

For two abstract polytopes P and Q (with rank(Q) = rank(P) + 1, say, or more generally for which the amalgamation makes sense), the amalgamation class ⟨P, Q⟩ is defined as the class of all abstract polytopes R whose facets are isomorphic to P and whose vertex-figures are isomorphic to Q.

Problem. Classify all pairs of abstract polytopes (P, Q) such that:
  (i) the amalgamation class ⟨P, Q⟩ is nonempty, and
  (ii) there exists a finite constant N = N(P, Q) such that every polytope R ∈ ⟨P, Q⟩ has at most N flag orbits under the action of its automorphism group (equivalently, the number of flag orbits of polytopes in ⟨P, Q⟩ is bounded).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears as an explicitly stated open problem in the literature on k-orbit polytopes. Related work (e.g., classifications of two-orbit and three-orbit polytopes, and results by Matteo on polytopes with few flag orbits) provides partial information for specific small flag-orbit counts, but no general classification of pairs (P, Q) yielding bounded flag-orbit amalgamation classes appears to be known.

status_evidence.title: Convex Polytopes and Tilings with Few Flag Orbits (Matteo)
status_evidence.snippet: Classifications of polytopes with small numbers of flag orbits (two-orbit, three-orbit) are developed but the general amalgamation question is not resolved.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial classifications by small flag-orbit count exist; no general classification of amalgamation classes with bounded flag-orbit number is given.

status_evidence.title: Two-Orbit Polytopes (Hubard)
status_evidence.snippet: Two-orbit polytopes of rank n fall into 2^{n-1} classes; structural results, not amalgamation classification.
status_evidence.claim: Existing work addresses two-orbit polytopes rather than the bounded-orbit amalgamation classification.

status_evidence.title: Symmetry of Polytopes and Polyhedra (Schulte, Handbook chapter 18)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys the amalgamation problem for regular abstract polytopes; the general amalgamation problem remains a central open area.
status_evidence.claim: The amalgamation problem for abstract polytopes is a central, broadly open area.
